title: An AI-Based OSSE Framework to Evaluate Learned Physical Consistency: A Multi-Model Study Using FourCastNet, Aurora, Prithvi WxC, and GraphCast
abstract: arXiv:2611.22024v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Observing System Simulation Experiments (OSSEs) are a central methodology for evaluating future atmospheric observing systems. We present the first AI-based OSSE framework to test whether different AI weather models can reproduce comparable physical impact from new observations that traditional physics based models generate. We evaluate four distinct architectural AI models on the Charney conjecture that incomplete historical observations can infer the present state of the atmospheric. We considner- FourCastNet V2, GraphCast, Aurora and Prithvi WxC and integrate each autoregressively over a 60-day forecast horizon. After a 30-day spin-up, we insert ERA5 temperature fields to infer winds and related atmospheric fields. Similar OSSE experiments are conducted for wind insertion. We measure the performance of each model's response to observational information on a 30-day data assimilation cycle forecast with and without data insertion. Disti

translated_title: 一种基于AI的OSSE框架用于评估学习到的物理一致性：使用FourCastNet、Aurora、Prithvi WxC和GraphCast的多模型研究
translated_abstract: 观测系统模拟实验（OSSE）是评估未来大气观测系统的核心方法。我们提出了首个基于AI的OSSE框架，用于测试不同的AI天气模型能否复现传统物理基模型对新观测所产生的相当物理影响。我们围绕Charney猜想（即不完整的历史观测可以推断大气的当前状态）对四种不同架构的AI模型进行了评估。我们考虑了FourCastNet V2、GraphCast、Aurora和Prithvi WxC，并将每个模型自回归地积分至60天的预报时长。经过30天的预热期（spin-up）后，我们插入ERA5温度场来推断风场及相关大气场。对于风场插入也开展了类似的OSSE实验。我们在有无数据插入的30天数据同化循环预报中，衡量每个模型对观测信息响应的性能。
tldr: 本文提出首个基于AI的观测系统模拟实验（OSSE）框架，通过Charney猜想评估四种不同架构的AI天气模型（FourCastNet V2、GraphCast、Aurora、Prithvi WxC）能否像传统物理模型一样对新观测产生相当的物理响应。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first AI-based OSSE framework, evaluating whether four architecturally distinct AI weather models (FourCastNet V2, GraphCast, Aurora, and Prithvi WxC) can reproduce physical impacts from new observations comparable to those of traditional physics-based models, tested through the Charney conjecture.
